answer: A quadratic entry fee ties cost to funding origin: the k-th account seeded from the same source pays k^2 times the base fee. At 1 POA base, an attacker trying to forge 1,000 accounts from one wallet pays about 333.8M POA, while an honest user with one account pays 1. A falcon auditor traces deposits on-chain; concealed shared funding burns the bond of every linked account and removes the source from the ivory list of trusted origins. Colluders cannot split the bill, since pooling funds into one wallet resets nothing and raises k.
